question: Goal-directed fluid therapy (GDFT) using stroke volume variation (SVV) is more reliable at guiding fluid administration in a spontaneously breathing patient than in a mechanically ventilated patient.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. SVV is a dynamic measure of heart-lung interaction that requires consistent, controlled ventilation to be interpreted reliably. Spontaneous breathing invalidates it.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Actually, this statement is false. SVV-based GDFT is most reliable in mechanically ventilated patients with regular tidal volumes (>8 mL/kg) and sinus rhythm. Spontaneous breathing generates irregular intrathoracic pressure changes that invalidate SVV as a fluid-responsiveness predictor.
